summary: Cupola cabin built 1928 on Sauk Mountain (Skagit Co.), flat cab 1957-58, removed by the Forest Service in 1986; hikers still reach the summit.

facts.design: cupola cabin (1928), replaced by an R-6 flat cab
facts.status_note: Lookout removed by the Forest Service in 1986 (the register says 1991); the summit is a hiking destination.

staffing.status: manned in 1953 (Philip Whalen); no later staffing found

access.note: Maintained Forest Service trail 613, heavily used; trailhead road described as fine for ordinary cars in June 2026.

visit.trail_note: About 4.2 miles round trip with 1,200 feet of gain from the trailhead off Highway 20.

events.note: Cupola cabin, the first lookout building on the site
Used as Aircraft Warning Service station 'Yoke 6-5' during WWII
Aircraft Warning Service station inactivated 16 Oct 1943; Forest Service kept the site for fire detection
Flat-top cab and tower built per Willhite; helicopter lift of material in Aug 1957 per Arlington Times item
R-6 flat cab per the register and firelookout.com (date differs from Willhite's 1957)
Lookout removed by the Forest Service, due to vandalism per 2013 trip report
Register gives 1991 as the removal year; most other sources say 1986
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, April 24, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say 1958; Willhite says 1957, and the Arlington Times item shows a helicopter lift in August 1957 to build a new lookout. The story gives both dates and does not pick one.
Willhite, the 2013 and 2026 trip reports and the Forest Service trail page point to 1986 or the 1980s; the register says 1991. The story uses 1986 and names the register's date.
The 2013 trip report body says 1938, but the same page's comment calls that a typo for 1928, which matches the register, firelookout.com and Willhite. The story uses 1928.

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict on the flat cab (1957 vs 1958) and on removal (1986 vs the register's 1991). The 2026 trip report is a personal account and the only source naming the steel cross; nothing read says when it was placed or who placed it. A Facebook post surfaced in search (not readable, so not cited) describes footings, cables and a cross at the summit; an editor could check it. A SummitPost search snippet also says Whalen spent 1953 there (unread, not cited). The Forest Service trail page carries site alerts for Mt. Baker Highway and Forest Service Road 41 timber closures; whether they affect the Sauk trailhead route was not checked, so the access note stays general.
